questions.prompt: Snellman opens by linking trigonometry to real-world tech such as:
questions.explain: He cites noise-canceling headphones as a trig application.

questions.prompt: A right triangle, in his definition, has:
questions.explain: Right triangle = one interior angle of 90°.

questions.prompt: Besides 3-4-5, which special right triangle does he highlight with integer sides?

choices: A Sine, cosine, and tangent ratios.

questions.prompt: How does Snellman remember that cosecant is 1/sine while secant is 1/cosine?
choices: A Cosecant starts with C, so it is 1 over the trig function that does not start with C (sine); secant starts with S, so 1 over cosine.
B Cosecant is always opposite over adjacent.
C Secant equals sine by definition.
questions.explain: His mnemonic: csc starts with C → 1/sine; sec starts with S → 1/cosine.
